turns.user_utterance: I bought something while traveling abroad, and the amount shown on my app is not the same as what I actually paid.
turns.assistant_response: Sorry about that—was the difference caused by the foreign exchange rate (the converted amount in your app), or did you also notice extra charges/fees? If you can tell me whether the merchant used a DCC (“Dynamic Currency Conversion”) option at checkout, that will help me pinpoint it.

turns.user_utterance: I think they used the DCC option, because the price was shown in my home currency at the checkout. No extra fees I saw.
turns.assistant_response:
Got it—if the price was shown in your home currency at checkout, that’s typically DCC, which can use a less favorable exchange rate. Your card payment may still be correct, but the app shows the converted amount based on the DCC rate/merchant conversion.

To check what happened on your side, can you share the currency your card was charged in and the home-currency amount you see in the app (plus the merchant’s displayed home-currency amount, if you have it)?
